readings.text: קֹדֶשׁ (shin dot not clearly seen; see marks)
readings.marks: There is a dot above, at the upper left of the qof roof, between qof and dalet. It reads as a holam on the qof. The long vertical stroke below the qof is the qof's own descender, not a vowel. The triangle of three dots (two above, one below) sits to the left of that descender, under the dalet, so it is a segol on the dalet. The qof has no vowel underneath. The shin's right head is heavy and blobby, so I can't tell whether there is a separate shin dot.
readings.confidence: high for the holam on the qof and segol on the dalet; low for the shin dot

readings.text: וירוּשָׁלַיִם (letters ו י ר ו ש ל י ם)
readings.marks: Vav, then yod. The second vav has a dot on its left side, which is a shuruk. Shin has a dot at its upper right, which is a shin dot. The mark under the shin looks like a qamats. A short mark under the lamed reads as a patah or qamats. Between the lamed's body and the final mem there seems to be a small letter-sized yod at the top of the line, not just a dot below it. I read that as a real yod. There is also a mark below at about that position, possibly a hiriq, and a vertical tick that may be a meteg. The first word's opening vav and yod have long descenders.
readings.confidence: medium on the yod being a real letter; low on the exact vowels below the lamed and yod
